title: Competition Bureau examining marketing practices by Gap, Old Navy

image.caption: An Old Navy location is seen in the Greater Toronto Area. Canada's competition watchdog is looking into the marketing practices of both Gap and Old Navy stores. (David MacIntosh/CBC)

blocks.text: The Competition Bureau is moving ahead with an investigation into whether clothing giants Gap and Old Navy are violating marketing regulations by making potentially false or misleading claims in their advertising.
Probe focusing on whether regular prices are inflated when items are on sale and the use of urgency cues

The federal Competition Bureau is moving ahead with an investigation into whether clothing giants Gap and Old Navy are violating marketing regulations by making potentially false or misleading claims in their advertising.

The competition watchdog has been granted a court order for information it says will help it determine whether the retailers are supplying customers with genuine regular prices when advertising items as on sale.
It is also examining the retailers' use of so-called urgency cues — messages such as ''Selling Fast'' or ''Only a Few Left'' — that pop up on their sites while consumers are browsing.

items: When is a deal really a deal? We tracked prices at Old Navy and Canadian Tire to find out

blocks.text: Old Navy and Gap are both owned by Gap Inc. and operate both online and bricks and mortar stores nationally.
CBC News has reached out to Gap Inc. for comment about the investigation.

The bureau says it took action after it saw a surge in complaints last year about allegedly inflated regular prices. At the time, it published a warning to remind businesses of their obligations under the Competition Act.
It adds that its ongoing investigation has yet to find any instances of wrongdoing.
